summary: Backend + frontend tested for the 3 NEW features (Orders, Leaderboard, Beat Plan). Backend: 11/12 pytest cases passed (see /app/backend/tests/test_fmcg_new_features.py). Frontend (mobile 390x844): all 3 new screens load and work end-to-end. Orders screen shows Total ₹2,969 / Uncollected ₹2,469, filter chips (All/Pending/Paid/Partial) work, tapping a status pill cycled Pending → Paid and persisted (Local Grocer's outstanding was reduced accordingly — verified via customers GET). Leaderboard renders 2 salesmen with rank medals, visits, sales and 'X orders' subtext; period segmented control (Today/This Week/This Month) switches data. John's My Day > 'Beat Plan' CTA opens beat-plan screen; '+' opens shop picker (correctly scoped to John's 3 customers), tap-to-add works, up/down reorder works, remove (x) works, progress card updated 0/1 → 1/2 correctly, 'Log a Visit' navigates to /visit/new. FOUND 1 REAL BUG: POST /api/beat-plan does not validate customer ownership — a salesman can save a beat plan containing another salesman's customer, and it renders on their Beat screen (proof: my test posted Priya's 'Electronics Hub' into John's plan and it displayed on the UI). Backend scoping must be enforced. Regression: PATCH /api/orders auto-updates customer.outstanding correctly on Pending→Paid and Paid→Pending. Salesman is 403 on another salesman's order. Leaderboard is 403 for salesman. Deprecated packages: none detected (no expo-av / expo-barcode-scanner / expo-background-fetch). Only non-blocking RN-web 'shadow*' deprecation warnings (already reported in iteration_1).

critical.issue: Does not validate customer ownership. A salesman can persist a plan containing customers owned by another salesman; _build_beat_stops then returns those foreign stops in GET and they render on the salesman UI. Spec explicitly requires: 'a salesman can only build a plan of their own customers'. Fix: in set_beat_plan, filter body.customer_ids to those where db.customers.find_one({_id: OID(cid), salesman_id: str(user._id)}) exists when role=='salesman' (or 400 if any cid is foreign). Reference: /app/backend/server.py:869-879.

minor.issue: Uses max(0, outstanding+delta) — clamping is safe for negative outstanding but hides accounting errors. Consider logging when clamp is hit.

integration_issues.issue: Because backend does not enforce ownership on POST /api/beat-plan, foreign customers show up as stops on the salesman's Beat screen (e.g. 'Electronics Hub' — South — appeared on John's beat). Frontend picker itself is correctly scoped, so this can only be triggered via direct API abuse — but still a real data-leak.

issues: Up/down arrow tap targets look ~24px; ideally 44x44 per iOS HIG for accessibility.

action_items: Enforce salesman ownership in POST /api/beat-plan: for role='salesman', reject or silently drop customer_ids that don't belong to the caller (or return 403). Add a regression test that mirrors test_salesman_can_only_plan_own_customers.
(Optional) Increase up/down/remove hit-slop or size to ≥44x44 on beat-plan stop cards for a11y.
(Optional, carried over from iter1) Migrate 'shadow*' style props to boxShadow — cosmetic RN-web deprecation warning.

server.py:813 _build_beat_stops resolves any customer_id passed in — no salesman_id filter — so it will leak whatever set_beat_plan stored.

rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/beat-plan accepts arbitrary customer_ids without validating that each belongs to the calling salesman. Reproduction: 1) Login as john (john@fmcg.com/sales123). 2) POST /api/beat-plan with {date: today, customer_ids: [ANY priya customer id]}. 3) GET /api/beat-plan → foreign stop is returned. 4) Salesman UI (My Day > Beat Plan) renders it. Mitigation: in `set_beat_plan`, if user.role=='salesman', run a single query `db.customers.find({_id: {$in: [OID(c) for c in body.customer_ids]}, salesman_id: str(user._id)})` and keep only those ids (or 403 on first foreign id). Also good to defensively filter inside `_build_beat_stops` for salesmen.
